designs.notes: Simulation (cocotb on Icarus Verilog 12, one recorded pytest run) and out-of-context Vivado 2026.1 results only. No board run, no MAC of the 96 design in the simulation, no real TCP peer, no real exchange; every order is synthetic. Requirements that need those are hooks and show as not run.

requirements.text: For any connection state and order, the block sends 15 words (113 bytes without the frame check sequence) whose bytes equal the Python reference, with sequence number, acknowledgement number, window and IP identification captured at the go edge, the SoupBinTCP Unsequenced Data packet of brief 110 as payload, no TCP options and the PSH and ACK flags, including sequence numbers at the 32-bit wrap.
requirements.title: Each order leaves as one complete 113-byte Ethernet, IPv4 and TCP frame, byte exact against the reference

requirements.text: The IPv4 header checksum and the TCP checksum of every segment sent equal the reference's, which is itself checked against outside vectors (RFC 1071, a published IPv4 header), including carries in the fold, sums that wrap, a TCP checksum that comes out 0 and a segment whose headers sum to all ones. This is checked by simulation of chosen and random cases; the all-inputs statements are B119-F-CKSUM-IP, -TCP and -MODEL.
requirements.title: Both checksums on the wire are the RFC 1071 checksums, at the corner cases

requirements.text: One record (rec_v, rec_seq, rec_len, rec_id, rec_pay) for each unpoisoned segment in the clock of its last word, and none for a poisoned one, so software can retransmit from the records; a segment dropped on the wire is retransmitted by software with the same bytes.
requirements.title: Every segment that left is handed back to software, and none that was poisoned

requirements.text: Handshake, SoupBinTCP login, orders, acknowledgements, a dropped segment, heartbeats, a small window and a rejected login all behave as the software side documents, with the exchange seeing every order exactly once and in order.
requirements.title: A Python TCP owner and a software OUCH exchange run a whole session through the block

requirements.text: Verilator -Wall over tcp_fast.sv and the frame builder inside it reports no warnings, with the waivers in lint/lint_waivers.vlt.
requirements.title: The RTL lints clean

requirements.text: With tcp_fast in place of ouch_enter, brief 110's path against brief 110's reference model sends the same orders, with the same payload bytes, valid checksums and gapless sequence numbers; speculative orders that the risk logic refuses leave poisoned.
requirements.title: The block replaces the order port of brief 110 and works behind its risk logic

requirements.text: Writes to static fields invalidate the template and are ignored and counted while a segment is in flight; live fields are accepted at any time and restart the staleness age; reads show the registers before the next edge; unmapped addresses read 0; the 14 counters count what the datasheet says and clear on CLR_CNT.
requirements.title: The register bus and counters behave as the datasheet states

requirements.text: An abort at any of edges 1 to 14 ends the frame with o_poison, leaves SND_NXT and IP_ID as before and produces no record; an abort at edge 0 cancels the go; a speculative segment with no verdict by edge 14 is poisoned; an abort wins over a commit; an abort after the frame left is late, counted and ignored.
requirements.title: An aborted or unverdicted segment is poisoned and consumes no sequence space

requirements.text: Checked in the order busy, not armed, template not valid or state stale, window closed, MSS below 59, an order is refused with the matching code and counter, nothing leaves and no state changes; a window of exactly 59 bytes admits one segment and one byte less admits none.
requirements.title: The block refuses to send when it is not armed, stale, window-closed, too small or busy

requirements.text: Hardware and software share one sequence space. After a heartbeat takes it and gives it back, after an abort, after a refusal and after a retransmission, the peer's received stream has no gap and no duplicate, and nothing is sent by software while the block is armed and idle.
requirements.title: The peer sees no gap and no duplicate in the sequence space

requirements.text: The block sums the payload words ouch_enter actually emits and compares the total with the early one the checksum used; a difference (for example a configuration change in flight) poisons the segment and counts sumerr, so a wrong checksum is never sent as valid.
requirements.title: A segment whose payload disagrees with the checksum that was sent is poisoned

requirements.text: Every one of the seeded faults of verif/mutants.yaml that builds fails the bench (mutation score 100 percent, 73 of 73). The set is the agent's own; whether it is wide enough is the human's check.
requirements.title: A seeded fault anywhere in the checksum, segment, verdict, refusal or register logic is caught

requirements.text: Brief 119's tcp_fast.sv builds the IPv4 header checksum from a precomputed template plus the changing fields. For all TTL, address and identification values it equals the complement of the ones' complement sum of the header, and the filled-in header sums to 0xFFFF.
requirements.title: The IPv4 header checksum of the TCP fast path equals the Internet checksum, for all inputs

requirements.text: For all addresses, ports, sequence and acknowledgement numbers, windows and payloads of up to 30 sixteen-bit words, the checksum the RTL equations produce equals the complement of the ones' complement sum over pseudo-header, header and payload. The byte-pair swapping, the streaming receive check and the timing are not modelled.
requirements.title: The TCP checksum of the TCP fast path equals the Internet checksum, for all inputs and payloads up to 30 words

requirements.text: The ones' complement sum of any list of 16-bit words equals the natural-number sum reduced mod 65535, and RFC 1624 equation 3 (incremental update) is correct for a header of any length when the new header is not all zero words; for an all-zero header it gives 0x0000. No current RTL patches a checksum in place; this is the arithmetic the fast path's template-plus-fields form relies on.
requirements.title: The ones' complement arithmetic the checksum equations rest on is correct, for lists of any length

designs.notes: Variants. Unless a requirement says otherwise, "the default build" is RATE_MATCH = 0 (the board-proven 97C receive path) and "the rate-matched build" is rm_gp (RATE_MATCH = 1, RM_OWN = 1). Board evidence is one KR260 on a short optical loopback; nothing has run against a network card. Briefs 112 (UVM bench) and 115 (SVA and formal proofs) are not merged: their items are hooks with no evidence, shown as not run.

requirements.text: Scrambler, block encode and decode, gearbox and block lock produce the same bits as the bit-serial Python reference, at every bit offset, with idles, ordered sets and bit-error runs.
requirements.title: PCS encodes and decodes 64B/66B bit-exactly against an independent model

requirements.text: Frames start in lane 0 and lane 4, every terminate lane and every length residue is handled, FCS is generated and checked, and a bad FCS is counted.
requirements.title: 64-bit MAC frames correctly in both directions

requirements.text: The receive gearbox slips to the block boundary from any offset, and a run of bit errors loses lock only above the documented threshold.
requirements.title: Block lock is acquired from any bit offset and survives bit errors

requirements.text: At least 100 receive-datapath restarts on the board, each one locks and no restart corrupts a frame.
requirements.title: The link locks after every receive-datapath restart

requirements.text: With RATE_MATCH = 0 the core is equivalent to the core of main 6909e43f (brief 97C) and passes that brief's bench.
requirements.title: The default build keeps the board-proven receive path

requirements.text: The elastic buffer inserts and deletes idles only between frames, never under- or overflows silently, and every order sent is fired and passes its content check.
requirements.title: Rate matching never corrupts a frame

requirements.external: a second reference clock or a 10G network card (a loopback has no frequency offset)
requirements.text: For any constant receive clock offset from -300 to +300 ppm relative to the transmit clock, no frame is lost or corrupted and the buffer neither overflows nor underflows. IEEE 802.3 allows +-100 ppm at each end, so two compliant ends differ by at most 200 ppm; +-300 ppm gives margin. A loopback has no offset, so a board test needs a second reference clock or another device on the link.
requirements.title: Rate matching holds under a real frequency offset

requirements.text: The PCS and MAC exchange frames with an independent 10GBASE-R implementation. A PCS talking to itself accepts its own symmetric mistakes, so only another implementation proves the block formats and scrambler order.
requirements.title: Interoperates with a standard 10GBASE-R network card

requirements.text: Every armed decision yields exactly one order, a poisoned order never fires, and every fault counter stays 0.
requirements.title: Orders are sent only for valid decisions, none is lost or poisoned

requirements.text: A stale counter, a missing order, a counter that was not read, a wrong polarity or a link that never came up fails the run and names the cause; unsafe actions are refused without the lock.
requirements.title: The board drivers cannot report OK when a safety check fails

requirements.text: tx_disable is 1 at reset; the board run switches the laser on only after the polarity was read back.
requirements.title: The laser is off at reset and its polarity is confirmed

requirements.text: Die temperature, VCCINT, VCCAUX and VCCBRAM read from SYSMON are inside the DS925 windows at the start and end of every board run.
requirements.title: Board runs stay inside the recommended operating conditions

requirements.text: report_cdc shows no Critical item and every crossing has the documented synchroniser structure.
requirements.title: No critical clock-domain crossing

requirements.text: Every address in regmap.py is decoded, nothing else is, vector widths agree, and the datasheet states unmapped reads return 0, counters read from a snapshot and reads have no side effects.
requirements.title: The register map is generated from one source and decoded exactly

requirements.text: The build files set parameters the core has, the base build keeps the 97C defaults, and each variant differs from the base only where documented.
requirements.title: Every build variant sets only the parameters it documents

requirements.text: es_ctrl aborts a point on a DRP timeout, latches the point at start, restores every DRP word and is absent when EYESCAN = 0.
requirements.title: The eye-scan sequencer drives the GT's DRP as its Python twin does

performance.quantity: frames lost in a line-rate burst

requirements.text: A burst at line rate loses no frame. Nothing has been measured; the line and payload rates stand on configuration and gearbox arithmetic only.
requirements.title: Line-rate throughput without loss

requirements.text: The write and read pointers of rate_match_gp count modulo 2^CW and cross by gray code. For every width CW > 0 and every value, the gray codes of b and b + 1 (including the wrap from 2^CW - 1 to 0) differ in exactly one bit, so a sample taken while the pointer moves is the old or the new code.
requirements.title: A pointer's gray code changes in exactly one bit per count, at every width

requirements.text: For every width and value, the decoder of the pointer crossing returns the count the encoder was given; and a sampled code that is the old or the new code decodes to the old or the new count.
requirements.title: Gray decoding inverts gray encoding, at every width

designs.notes: Arithmetic library, function adder (brief 139a). Everything here is before Vivado: the model, the RTL variants, simulation, formal equivalence, Lean statements and the prepared out-of-context build files. No performance requirement exists because nothing about LUTs, DSPs, Fmax or power has been measured yet; the Vivado runs (build/<variant>/build.yaml) will add them. Every requirement is a draft written by the agent; none is agreed by a human. Lean statements are not approved. Generated by arith/tools/gen_testplan.py.

requirements.text: arith/adder/model.py gives, for every input, the result that spec.md defines. It agrees with an independent formulation (a bit-serial chain of full adders) on every input at small widths and with Python's integer arithmetic on random large-width inputs, and the conventions that a user could guess wrong (spec.md, last section) are pinned by examples.
requirements.title: The bit-exact model is right

requirements.text: At every parameter point listed in spec.yaml (16 exhaustive points, 14 random ones, across 3 variants), each variant's outputs equal the model's in every clock: every input is driven at the small points; edge values, runs of ones, and random inputs at the large ones. The function is exact, so there is no error bound.
requirements.title: Every variant is bit-exact against the model

requirements.text: Each variant's latency in clocks is the expression in spec.yaml (ripple: 0; carry_select: 0; pipelined: STAGES), and the bench, run with a latency two clocks off, fails for every variant, so the passing runs prove the latency rather than assume it.
requirements.title: Latency is as specified and the bench would notice if it were not

requirements.text: SymbiYosys with the slang front end checks the variants against each other and a plain reference (a single `+` or `*`, or the specification written as RTL). The jobs in formal/jobs.yaml name the widths; a proof is by k-induction (for all inputs, any run length) at the widths listed there, a bounded check holds only to its stated depth. Widths beyond the listed ones are covered by simulation, not by proof.
requirements.title: The variants are equivalent to a plain reference, by proof where the tools allow

requirements.text: Every one of the mutants in verif/mutants.yaml (one exact text change each, in the variant's RTL: an inverted condition, a wrong constant, a dropped connection, a lost reset) makes the cocotb bench fail; mutants that survive or do not build are reported, never hidden.
requirements.title: The bench catches seeded faults

requirements.text: arith/adder/harness holds the model, the cocotb bench, a SystemVerilog checker, coverage targets and a runner that needs nothing else from the repository. Run standalone against every variant (one small exhaustive point and one large random point each, with the checker beside the instance) it passes and the random runs meet every coverage target; run against a planted fault it fails, with and without the checker. Its generated files are the repository's own bench, so they cannot drift.
requirements.title: The packaged verification harness is a standalone deliverable that works

requirements.text: spec.yaml states an interface contract (protocol, throughput, latency, reset, clock, stalls) and integration guidance (port timing, constraints to carry). Everything here is before Vivado: the model, the RTL variants, simulation, formal equivalence, Lean statements and the prepared out-of-context build files. No performance requirement exists because nothing about LUTs, DSPs, Fmax or power has been measured yet; the Vivado runs (build/<variant>/build.yaml) will add them. Every requirement is a draft written by the agent; none is agreed by a human. Lean statements are not approved. Generated by arith/tools/gen_testplan.py.

requirements.text: arith/sincos/model.py gives, for every input, the result that spec.md defines. It agrees with an independent formulation (an exact rational (Fraction) evaluation of the interpolation formula, a floating-point CORDIC, and the maths library's sin and cos) on every input at small widths and with Python's integer arithmetic on random large-width inputs, and the conventions that a user could guess wrong (spec.md, last section) are pinned by examples.
requirements.title: The bit-exact model is right

requirements.text: At every parameter point listed in spec.yaml (16 exhaustive points, 9 random ones, across 3 variants), each variant's outputs equal its own model's (model.py, selected by variant) in every clock: every input is driven at the small points; edge values, table break points and random inputs at the large ones. The variants round differently and are not bit-identical to each other; the model of each is the bit-exact definition of that variant, and its distance from the exact function is the accuracy requirement.
requirements.title: Every variant is bit-exact against its own model

requirements.text: Each of the 9 accuracy points of spec.yaml states a bound in last places; the model's error against the exact function (the maths library, real arithmetic, unrounded) over EVERY input of that point is at most the bound and within 0.06 of it (so the bound is neither false nor loose). A point not listed has no stated bound.
requirements.title: The error against the exact function is within the stated bound, at every listed point

requirements.text: Each variant's latency in clocks is the expression in spec.yaml (lerp: 2; poly2: 3; cordic: NIT), and the bench, run with a latency two clocks off, fails for every variant, so the passing runs prove the latency rather than assume it.
requirements.title: Latency is as specified and the bench would notice if it were not

requirements.text: SymbiYosys with the slang front end compares each variant, delayed by its latency, with the exact function on 8 input bits to 24 fractional bits (a reference ROM written from the maths library, formal/*_ref.sv) and asserts the error stays within the bound of the job, which is the model's measured error at that point plus one unit for the reference's own rounding. A proof is by k-induction (for all inputs, any run length) at the widths in formal/jobs.yaml; wider points are covered by the exhaustive scan of the accuracy requirement and by simulation, not by proof. The quadrant map and the variants' structural identities are inside the checks.
requirements.title: The error against the exact function is bounded for all inputs, by proof, at a small input width

requirements.text: Every one of the mutants in verif/mutants.yaml (one exact text change each, in the variant's RTL: an inverted condition, a wrong constant, a dropped connection, a lost reset) makes the cocotb bench fail; mutants that survive or do not build are reported, never hidden.
requirements.title: The bench catches seeded faults

requirements.text: arith/sincos/harness holds the model, the cocotb bench, a SystemVerilog checker, coverage targets and a runner that needs nothing else from the repository. Run standalone against every variant (one small exhaustive point and one large random point each, with the checker beside the instance) it passes and the random runs meet every coverage target; run against a planted fault it fails, with and without the checker. Its generated files are the repository's own bench, so they cannot drift.
requirements.title: The packaged verification harness is a standalone deliverable that works

requirements.text: spec.yaml states an interface contract (protocol, throughput, latency, reset, clock, stalls) and integration guidance (port timing, constraints to carry). Every variant passes Verilator -Wall at every point of spec.yaml; its ports and default parameters are the ones spec.yaml states; its header states the intended primitive use before any Vivado run; spec.md is the rendering of spec.yaml; the out-of-context wrapper and the build.yaml for each variant (Artix-7 xc7a100t and K26 xck26, prepared and not run) are current and lint-clean at every point they list, so a Vivado run can start from the repository alone.
requirements.title: The RTL is lint-clean, and its files agree with the specification and with the Vivado build files

requirements.source: arith/sincos/rtl/sincos_lerp.sv (the bit-field split of the phase)
requirements.text: For every width k, a phase below 4 * 2^k splits into a quadrant (its top two bits) below 4 and an angle (the rest) so that quadrant * 2^k + angle is the phase again. The statement is the specification and is NOT approved by a human (verif/lean_approvals.yaml is empty), so the proof is shown but not counted as verification. The Lean text is a hand transcription of the RTL's structure; it models no timing or clocking.
requirements.title: The phase splits into a quadrant and an angle without loss, for every width

requirements.source: arith/sincos/rtl/sincos_lerp.sv (the bit-field split of the phase)
requirements.text: For every width k, any quadrant and any angle below 2^k put together split back into the same quadrant and the same angle: the split is a bijection. The statement is the specification and is NOT approved by a human (verif/lean_approvals.yaml is empty), so the proof is shown but not counted as verification. The Lean text is a hand transcription of the RTL's structure; it models no timing or clocking.
requirements.title: Every quadrant and angle pair is one phase, for every width

requirements.source: arith/sincos/rtl/sincos_lerp.sv (the product, sum and shift lines of the interpolation)
requirements.text: In a rising segment with break-point value c0 and slope s, the interpolated value (c0 * 2^D + s * d) / 2^D lies between c0 and c0 + s for every position d below 2^D and every D: the table variant cannot overshoot its segment. The statement is the specification and is NOT approved by a human (verif/lean_approvals.yaml is empty), so the proof is shown but not counted as verification. The Lean text is a hand transcription of the RTL's structure; it models no timing or clocking.
requirements.title: Linear interpolation stays between the segment's end values, for every width

requirements.source: arith/sincos/rtl/sincos_cordic.sv (the x and y adders of one stage)
requirements.text: For every direction d = +-1 and every shift (scaled by u = 2^i), the step (u x - d y, u y + d x) multiplies x^2 + y^2 by exactly u^2 + 1, whatever the data: the CORDIC gain is a data-independent constant. The statement is the specification and is NOT approved by a human (verif/lean_approvals.yaml is empty), so the proof is shown but not counted as verification. The Lean text is a hand transcription of the RTL's structure; it models no timing or clocking.
requirements.title: A circular CORDIC step scales the squared length by a constant, for every width

designs.notes: Simulation (cocotb on Icarus Verilog 12, one recorded pytest run) and out-of-context Vivado 2026.1 results only. No board run, no MAC of the 96 design in the simulation, no real TCP peer, no real exchange; every order is synthetic. Requirements that need those are hooks and show as not run.

requirements.text: For any connection state and order, the block sends 15 words (113 bytes without the frame check sequence) whose bytes equal the Python reference, with sequence number, acknowledgement number, window and IP identification captured at the go edge, the SoupBinTCP Unsequenced Data packet of brief 110 as payload, no TCP options and the PSH and ACK flags, including sequence numbers at the 32-bit wrap.
requirements.title: Each order leaves as one complete 113-byte Ethernet, IPv4 and TCP frame, byte exact against the reference

requirements.text: The IPv4 header checksum and the TCP checksum of every segment sent equal the reference's, which is itself checked against outside vectors (RFC 1071, a published IPv4 header), including carries in the fold, sums that wrap, a TCP checksum that comes out 0 and a segment whose headers sum to all ones. This is checked by simulation of chosen and random cases; the all-inputs statements are B119-F-CKSUM-IP, -TCP and -MODEL.
requirements.title: Both checksums on the wire are the RFC 1071 checksums, at the corner cases

requirements.text: One record (rec_v, rec_seq, rec_len, rec_id, rec_pay) for each unpoisoned segment in the clock of its last word, and none for a poisoned one, so software can retransmit from the records; a segment dropped on the wire is retransmitted by software with the same bytes.
requirements.title: Every segment that left is handed back to software, and none that was poisoned

requirements.text: Handshake, SoupBinTCP login, orders, acknowledgements, a dropped segment, heartbeats, a small window and a rejected login all behave as the software side documents, with the exchange seeing every order exactly once and in order.
requirements.title: A Python TCP owner and a software OUCH exchange run a whole session through the block

requirements.text: Verilator -Wall over tcp_fast.sv and the frame builder inside it reports no warnings, with the waivers in lint/lint_waivers.vlt.
requirements.title: The RTL lints clean

requirements.text: With tcp_fast in place of ouch_enter, brief 110's path against brief 110's reference model sends the same orders, with the same payload bytes, valid checksums and gapless sequence numbers; speculative orders that the risk logic refuses leave poisoned.
requirements.title: The block replaces the order port of brief 110 and works behind its risk logic

requirements.text: Writes to static fields invalidate the template and are ignored and counted while a segment is in flight; live fields are accepted at any time and restart the staleness age; reads show the registers before the next edge; unmapped addresses read 0; the 14 counters count what the datasheet says and clear on CLR_CNT.
requirements.title: The register bus and counters behave as the datasheet states

requirements.text: An abort at any of edges 1 to 14 ends the frame with o_poison, leaves SND_NXT and IP_ID as before and produces no record; an abort at edge 0 cancels the go; a speculative segment with no verdict by edge 14 is poisoned; an abort wins over a commit; an abort after the frame left is late, counted and ignored.
requirements.title: An aborted or unverdicted segment is poisoned and consumes no sequence space

requirements.text: Checked in the order busy, not armed, template not valid or state stale, window closed, MSS below 59, an order is refused with the matching code and counter, nothing leaves and no state changes; a window of exactly 59 bytes admits one segment and one byte less admits none.
requirements.title: The block refuses to send when it is not armed, stale, window-closed, too small or busy

requirements.text: Hardware and software share one sequence space. After a heartbeat takes it and gives it back, after an abort, after a refusal and after a retransmission, the peer's received stream has no gap and no duplicate, and nothing is sent by software while the block is armed and idle.
requirements.title: The peer sees no gap and no duplicate in the sequence space

requirements.text: The block sums the payload words ouch_enter actually emits and compares the total with the early one the checksum used; a difference (for example a configuration change in flight) poisons the segment and counts sumerr, so a wrong checksum is never sent as valid.
requirements.title: A segment whose payload disagrees with the checksum that was sent is poisoned

requirements.text: Every one of the seeded faults of verif/mutants.yaml that builds fails the bench (mutation score 100 percent, 73 of 73). The set is the agent's own; whether it is wide enough is the human's check.
requirements.title: A seeded fault anywhere in the checksum, segment, verdict, refusal or register logic is caught

requirements.text: Brief 119's tcp_fast.sv builds the IPv4 header checksum from a precomputed template plus the changing fields. For all TTL, address and identification values it equals the complement of the ones' complement sum of the header, and the filled-in header sums to 0xFFFF.
requirements.title: The IPv4 header checksum of the TCP fast path equals the Internet checksum, for all inputs

requirements.text: For all addresses, ports, sequence and acknowledgement numbers, windows and payloads of up to 30 sixteen-bit words, the checksum the RTL equations produce equals the complement of the ones' complement sum over pseudo-header, header and payload. The byte-pair swapping, the streaming receive check and the timing are not modelled.
requirements.title: The TCP checksum of the TCP fast path equals the Internet checksum, for all inputs and payloads up to 30 words

requirements.text: The ones' complement sum of any list of 16-bit words equals the natural-number sum reduced mod 65535, and RFC 1624 equation 3 (incremental update) is correct for a header of any length when the new header is not all zero words; for an all-zero header it gives 0x0000. No current RTL patches a checksum in place; this is the arithmetic the fast path's template-plus-fields form relies on.
requirements.title: The ones' complement arithmetic the checksum equations rest on is correct, for lists of any length

designs.notes: Variants. Unless a requirement says otherwise, "the default build" is RATE_MATCH = 0 (the board-proven 97C receive path) and "the rate-matched build" is rm_gp (RATE_MATCH = 1, RM_OWN = 1). Board evidence is one KR260 on a short optical loopback; nothing has run against a network card. Briefs 112 (UVM bench) and 115 (SVA and formal proofs) are not merged: their items are hooks with no evidence, shown as not run.

requirements.text: Scrambler, block encode and decode, gearbox and block lock produce the same bits as the bit-serial Python reference, at every bit offset, with idles, ordered sets and bit-error runs.
requirements.title: PCS encodes and decodes 64B/66B bit-exactly against an independent model

requirements.text: Frames start in lane 0 and lane 4, every terminate lane and every length residue is handled, FCS is generated and checked, and a bad FCS is counted.
requirements.title: 64-bit MAC frames correctly in both directions

requirements.text: The receive gearbox slips to the block boundary from any offset, and a run of bit errors loses lock only above the documented threshold.
requirements.title: Block lock is acquired from any bit offset and survives bit errors

requirements.text: At least 100 receive-datapath restarts on the board, each one locks and no restart corrupts a frame.
requirements.title: The link locks after every receive-datapath restart

requirements.text: With RATE_MATCH = 0 the core is equivalent to the core of main 6909e43f (brief 97C) and passes that brief's bench.
requirements.title: The default build keeps the board-proven receive path

requirements.text: The elastic buffer inserts and deletes idles only between frames, never under- or overflows silently, and every order sent is fired and passes its content check.
requirements.title: Rate matching never corrupts a frame

requirements.external: a second reference clock or a 10G network card (a loopback has no frequency offset)
requirements.text: For any constant receive clock offset from -300 to +300 ppm relative to the transmit clock, no frame is lost or corrupted and the buffer neither overflows nor underflows. IEEE 802.3 allows +-100 ppm at each end, so two compliant ends differ by at most 200 ppm; +-300 ppm gives margin. A loopback has no offset, so a board test needs a second reference clock or another device on the link.
requirements.title: Rate matching holds under a real frequency offset

requirements.text: The PCS and MAC exchange frames with an independent 10GBASE-R implementation. A PCS talking to itself accepts its own symmetric mistakes, so only another implementation proves the block formats and scrambler order.
requirements.title: Interoperates with a standard 10GBASE-R network card

requirements.text: Every armed decision yields exactly one order, a poisoned order never fires, and every fault counter stays 0.
requirements.title: Orders are sent only for valid decisions, none is lost or poisoned

requirements.text: A stale counter, a missing order, a counter that was not read, a wrong polarity or a link that never came up fails the run and names the cause; unsafe actions are refused without the lock.
requirements.title: The board drivers cannot report OK when a safety check fails

requirements.text: tx_disable is 1 at reset; the board run switches the laser on only after the polarity was read back.
requirements.title: The laser is off at reset and its polarity is confirmed

requirements.text: Die temperature, VCCINT, VCCAUX and VCCBRAM read from SYSMON are inside the DS925 windows at the start and end of every board run.
requirements.title: Board runs stay inside the recommended operating conditions

requirements.text: report_cdc shows no Critical item and every crossing has the documented synchroniser structure.
requirements.title: No critical clock-domain crossing

requirements.text: Every address in regmap.py is decoded, nothing else is, vector widths agree, and the datasheet states unmapped reads return 0, counters read from a snapshot and reads have no side effects.
requirements.title: The register map is generated from one source and decoded exactly

requirements.text: The build files set parameters the core has, the base build keeps the 97C defaults, and each variant differs from the base only where documented.
requirements.title: Every build variant sets only the parameters it documents

requirements.text: es_ctrl aborts a point on a DRP timeout, latches the point at start, restores every DRP word and is absent when EYESCAN = 0.
requirements.title: The eye-scan sequencer drives the GT's DRP as its Python twin does

requirements.title: Line-rate throughput without loss

requirements.text: The write and read pointers of rate_match_gp count modulo 2^CW and cross by gray code. For every width CW > 0 and every value, the gray codes of b and b + 1 (including the wrap from 2^CW - 1 to 0) differ in exactly one bit, so a sample taken while the pointer moves is the old or the new code.
requirements.title: A pointer's gray code changes in exactly one bit per count, at every width

requirements.text: For every width and value, the decoder of the pointer crossing returns the count the encoder was given; and a sampled code that is the old or the new code decodes to the old or the new count.
requirements.title: Gray decoding inverts gray encoding, at every width

designs.notes: Arithmetic library, function adder (brief 139a). Everything here is before Vivado: the model, the RTL variants, simulation, formal equivalence, Lean statements and the prepared out-of-context build files. No performance requirement exists because nothing about LUTs, DSPs, Fmax or power has been measured yet; the Vivado runs (build/<variant>/build.yaml) will add them. Every requirement is a draft written by the agent; none is agreed by a human. Lean statements are not approved. Generated by arith/tools/gen_testplan.py.

requirements.text: arith/adder/model.py gives, for every input, the result that spec.md defines. It agrees with an independent formulation (a bit-serial chain of full adders) on every input at small widths and with Python's integer arithmetic on random large-width inputs, and the conventions that a user could guess wrong (spec.md, last section) are pinned by examples.
requirements.title: The bit-exact model is right

requirements.text: At every parameter point listed in spec.yaml (16 exhaustive points, 14 random ones, across 3 variants), each variant's outputs equal the model's in every clock: every input is driven at the small points; edge values, runs of ones, and random inputs at the large ones. The function is exact, so there is no error bound.
requirements.title: Every variant is bit-exact against the model

requirements.text: Each variant's latency in clocks is the expression in spec.yaml (ripple: 0; carry_select: 0; pipelined: STAGES), and the bench, run with a latency two clocks off, fails for every variant, so the passing runs prove the latency rather than assume it.
requirements.title: Latency is as specified and the bench would notice if it were not

requirements.text: SymbiYosys with the slang front end checks the variants against each other and a plain reference (a single `+` or `*`, or the specification written as RTL). The jobs in formal/jobs.yaml name the widths; a proof is by k-induction (for all inputs, any run length) at the widths listed there, a bounded check holds only to its stated depth. Widths beyond the listed ones are covered by simulation, not by proof.
requirements.title: The variants are equivalent to a plain reference, by proof where the tools allow

requirements.text: Every one of the mutants in verif/mutants.yaml (one exact text change each, in the variant's RTL: an inverted condition, a wrong constant, a dropped connection, a lost reset) makes the cocotb bench fail; mutants that survive or do not build are reported, never hidden.
requirements.title: The bench catches seeded faults

requirements.text: arith/adder/harness holds the model, the cocotb bench, a SystemVerilog checker, coverage targets and a runner that needs nothing else from the repository. Run standalone against every variant (one small exhaustive point and one large random point each, with the checker beside the instance) it passes and the random runs meet every coverage target; run against a planted fault it fails, with and without the checker. Its generated files are the repository's own bench, so they cannot drift.
requirements.title: The packaged verification harness is a standalone deliverable that works

requirements.text: spec.yaml states an interface contract (protocol, throughput, latency, reset, clock, stalls) and integration guidance (port timing, constraints to carry). Every variant passes Verilator -Wall at every point of spec.yaml; its ports and default parameters are the ones spec.yaml states; its header states the intended primitive use before any Vivado run; spec.md is the rendering of spec.yaml; the out-of-context wrapper and the build.yaml for each variant (Artix-7 xc7a100t and K26 xck26, prepared and not run) are current and lint-clean at every point they list, so a Vivado run can start from the repository alone.
requirements.title: The RTL is lint-clean, and its files agree with the specification and with the Vivado build files

requirements.text: A carry-select adder (a low block, and a high block computed for carry in 0 and 1 and selected by the low block's carry out) returns the same sum and carry out as plain addition, for every block widths m and k and every pair of operands. The statement is the specification and is NOT approved by a human (verif/lean_approvals.yaml is empty), so the proof is shown but not counted as verification. The Lean text is a hand transcription of the RTL's structure; it models no timing or clocking.

requirements.text: For every width n, a + ~b + ~bin on n bits equals a - b - bin modulo 2^n, and its carry out is 1 exactly when there is no borrow: the identity every variant's subtract path rests on. The statement is the specification and is NOT approved by a human (verif/lean_approvals.yaml is empty), so the proof is shown but not counted as verification. requirements.text: Each of the 3 accuracy points of spec.yaml states a bound in last places; the model's error against the exact function (the maths library, real arithmetic, unrounded) over EVERY input of that point is at most the bound and within 0.06 of it (so the bound is neither false nor loose). A proof is by k-induction (for all inputs, any run length) at the widths in formal/jobs.yaml; wider points are covered by the exhaustive scan of the accuracy requirement and by simulation, not by proof. No performance requirement exists because nothing about LUTs, DSPs, Fmax or power has been measured yet; the Vivado runs (build/<variant>/build.yaml) will add them. Every requirement is a draft written by the agent; none is agreed by a human. Lean statements are not approved. Generated by arith/tools/gen_testplan.py.

requirements.text: arith/multiplier/model.py gives, for every input, the result that spec.md defines. It agrees with an independent formulation (a shift-and-add formulation (and, for the Booth recoding, the digit-sum identity)) on every input at small widths and with Python's integer arithmetic on random large-width inputs, and the conventions that a user could guess wrong (spec.md, last section) are pinned by examples.
requirements.title: The bit-exact model is right

requirements.text: At every parameter point listed in spec.yaml (24 exhaustive points, 14 random ones, across 3 variants), each variant's outputs equal the model's in every clock: every input is driven at the small points; edge values, runs of ones, and random inputs at the large ones. The function is exact, so there is no error bound.
requirements.title: Every variant is bit-exact against the model

requirements.text: Each variant's latency in clocks is the expression in spec.yaml (dsp: STAGES; lut_array: REG; booth_r4: REG), and the bench, run with a latency two clocks off, fails for every variant, so the passing runs prove the latency rather than assume it.
requirements.title: Latency is as specified and the bench would notice if it were not

requirements.text: SymbiYosys with the slang front end checks the variants against each other and a plain reference (a single `+` or `*`, or the specification written as RTL). The jobs in formal/jobs.yaml name the widths; a proof is by k-induction (for all inputs, any run length) at the widths listed there, a bounded check holds only to its stated depth. Widths beyond the listed ones are covered by simulation, not by proof.
requirements.title: The variants are equivalent to a plain reference, by proof where the tools allow

requirements.text: Every one of the mutants in verif/mutants.yaml (one exact text change each, in the variant's RTL: an inverted condition, a wrong constant, a dropped connection, a lost reset) makes the cocotb bench fail; mutants that survive or do not build are reported, never hidden.
requirements.title: The bench catches seeded faults

requirements.text: arith/multiplier/harness holds the model, the cocotb bench, a SystemVerilog checker, coverage targets and a runner that needs nothing else from the repository. Run standalone against every variant (one small exhaustive point and one large random point each, with the checker beside the instance) it passes and the random runs meet every coverage target; run against a planted fault it fails, with and without the checker. Its generated files are the repository's own bench, so they cannot drift.
requirements.title: The packaged verification harness is a standalone deliverable that works

requirements.text: spec.yaml states an interface contract (protocol, throughput, latency, reset, clock, stalls) and integration guidance (port timing, constraints to carry). Every variant passes Verilator -Wall at every point of spec.yaml; its ports and default parameters are the ones spec.yaml states; its header states the intended primitive use before any Vivado run; spec.md is the rendering of spec.yaml; the out-of-context wrapper and the build.yaml for each variant (Artix-7 xc7a100t and K26 xck26, prepared and not run) are current and lint-clean at every point they list, so a Vivado run can start from the repository alone.
requirements.title: The RTL is lint-clean, and its files agree with the specification and with the Vivado build files

requirements.source: arith/multiplier/rtl/mult_booth_r4.sv (WBX, NP, bwide, bxe, the digit case table)
requirements.text: For every multiplier width, the radix-4 Booth digits d_i = -2 b[2i+1] + b[2i] + b[2i-1] of an even-length bit pattern sum, weighted by 4^i, to its two's-complement value. The statement is the specification and is NOT approved by a human (verif/lean_approvals.yaml is empty), so the proof is shown but not counted as verification. The Lean text is a hand transcription of the RTL's structure; it models no timing or clocking.
requirements.title: Radix-4 Booth digits sum to the multiplier's value, for every width

requirements.text: For every pattern whose top bit is 0 (an unsigned multiplier given the RTL's extra zero bit), the Booth digit sum equals the unsigned value. The statement is the specification and is NOT approved by a human (verif/lean_approvals.yaml is empty), so the proof is shown but not counted as verification. The Lean text is a hand transcription of the RTL's structure; it models no timing or clocking.
requirements.title: An unsigned multiplier extended by a zero bit has non-negative digits summing to its value, for every width

designs.notes: Arithmetic library, function sincos (brief 139d). Everything here is before Vivado: the model, the RTL variants, simulation, formal equivalence, Lean statements and the prepared out-of-context build files. No performance requirement exists because nothing about LUTs, DSPs, Fmax or power has been measured yet; the Vivado runs (build/<variant>/build.yaml) will add them. Every requirement is a draft written by the agent; none is agreed by a human. Lean statements are not approved. Generated by arith/tools/gen_testplan.py.

requirements.text: arith/sincos/model.py gives, for every input, the result that spec.md defines. It agrees with an independent formulation (an exact rational (Fraction) evaluation of the interpolation formula, a floating-point CORDIC, and the maths library's sin and cos) on every input at small widths and with Python's integer arithmetic on random large-width inputs, and the conventions that a user could guess wrong (spec.md, last section) are pinned by examples.
requirements.title: The bit-exact model is right

requirements.text: At every parameter point listed in spec.yaml (16 exhaustive points, 9 random ones, across 3 variants), each variant's outputs equal its own model's (model.py, selected by variant) in every clock: every input is driven at the small points; edge values, table break points and random inputs at the large ones. The variants round differently and are not bit-identical to each other; the model of each is the bit-exact definition of that variant, and its distance from the exact function is the accuracy requirement.
requirements.title: Every variant is bit-exact against its own model

requirements.text: Each of the 9 accuracy points of spec.yaml states a bound in last places; the model's error against the exact function (the maths library, real arithmetic, unrounded) over EVERY input of that point is at most the bound and within 0.06 of it (so the bound is neither false nor loose). A point not listed has no stated bound.
requirements.title: The error against the exact function is within the stated bound, at every listed point

requirements.text: Each variant's latency in clocks is the expression in spec.yaml (lerp: 2; poly2: 3; cordic: NIT), and the bench, run with a latency two clocks off, fails for every variant, so the passing runs prove the latency rather than assume it.
requirements.title: Latency is as specified and the bench would notice if it were not

requirements.text: SymbiYosys with the slang front end compares each variant, delayed by its latency, with the exact function on 8 input bits to 24 fractional bits (a reference ROM written from the maths library, formal/*_ref.sv) and asserts the error stays within the bound of the job, which is the model's measured error at that point plus one unit for the reference's own rounding. A proof is by k-induction (for all inputs, any run length) at the widths in formal/jobs.yaml; wider points are covered by the exhaustive scan of the accuracy requirement and by simulation, not by proof. The quadrant map and the variants' structural identities are inside the checks.
requirements.title: The error against the exact function is bounded for all inputs, by proof, at a small input width

requirements.source: arith/sincos/rtl/sincos_lerp.sv (the bit-field split of the phase)
requirements.text: For every width k, a phase below 4 * 2^k splits into a quadrant (its top two bits) below 4 and an angle (the rest) so that quadrant * 2^k + angle is the phase again. The statement is the specification and is NOT approved by a human (verif/lean_approvals.yaml is empty), so the proof is shown but not counted as verification. The Lean text is a hand transcription of the RTL's structure; it models no timing or clocking.
requirements.title: The phase splits into a quadrant and an angle without loss, for every width

requirements.source: arith/sincos/rtl/sincos_lerp.sv (the bit-field split of the phase)
requirements.text: For every width k, any quadrant and any angle below 2^k put together split back into the same quadrant and the same angle: the split is a bijection. The statement is the specification and is NOT approved by a human (verif/lean_approvals.yaml is empty), so the proof is shown but not counted as verification. The Lean text is a hand transcription of the RTL's structure; it models no timing or clocking.
requirements.title: Every quadrant and angle pair is one phase, for every width

requirements.source: arith/sincos/rtl/sincos_lerp.sv (the product, sum and shift lines of the interpolation)
requirements.text: In a rising segment with break-point value c0 and slope s, the interpolated value (c0 * 2^D + s * d) / 2^D lies between c0 and c0 + s for every position d below 2^D and every D: the table variant cannot overshoot its segment. The statement is the specification and is NOT approved by a human (verif/lean_approvals.yaml is empty), so the proof is shown but not counted as verification. The Lean text is a hand transcription of the RTL's structure; it models no timing or clocking.
requirements.title: Linear interpolation stays between the segment's end values, for every width

requirements.source: arith/sincos/rtl/sincos_cordic.sv (the x and y adders of one stage)
requirements.text: For every direction d = +-1 and every shift (scaled by u = 2^i), the step (u x - d y, u y + d x) multiplies x^2 + y^2 by exactly u^2 + 1, whatever the data: the CORDIC gain is a data-independent constant. The statement is the specification and is NOT approved by a human (verif/lean_approvals.yaml is empty), so the proof is shown but not counted as verification. The Lean text is a hand transcription of the RTL's structure; it models no timing or clocking.
requirements.title: A circular CORDIC step scales the squared length by a constant, for every width

content.framing: The human specifies the requirements and checks that the verification is thorough enough. The agent holds the knowledge to implement and to verify. You can open any of the implementation or the evidence, and you do not have to. Hardware on the board, with attached instruments, is a verification layer of its own: where a requirement depends on something outside the design (an optical link, a network card, a data source) it may be the only way to close it.
